subject: Next steps: stakeholder map & procurement path
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@fintrust.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Next steps: stakeholder map & procurement path

Hi Samantha — great conversation earlier. Quick recap + a couple asks so we can accelerate evaluation on your side.

Recap from our call:
- Use case: reduce inference cost for customer-facing summarization pipelines and improve p95 latency for long-context models.
- Primary workload: batched document summarization (avg 2–3k tokens) and near-real-time chat (200–600 tokens).
- Initial target: pilot with 3 services, then roll to 12 services in Q4.

What we need to unblock procurement & approval (can you help point to the right people?):
1) Org map / who signs: who would be the economic buyer for a cross-team inference platform purchase?
2) Security & legal contacts: who owns vendor security questionnaires (SOC 2 / data residency) and contract redlines?
3) Procurement steps: do you require an SOW, PO number upfront, or an approved vendor registry entry? Any standard forms?
4) Decision criteria: budget cadence, evaluation success metrics, and any mandatory compliance gates.

If it’s easiest, a quick attachment with names/roles and rough signing authority is perfect. I can turn this into a 1-page mutual action plan for your team.

Attachments: example MAP template (I can share a populated version once we have names).

Thanks — I’ll follow up in a couple of days if I don’t hear back.

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@fintrust.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@fintrust.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Next steps: stakeholder map & procurement path

Logan — thanks for the clear recap, that helps. See answers below and I attached our current org chart.

Quick answers:
- Economic buyer: Maria Alvarez, VP of Product (Maria.Alvarez@fintrust.com). She owns vendor spend for product-related infra.
- Security & legal: Tom Li (cc’d) handles vendor security questionnaires and contract redlines. He’ll want to see SOC 2 + data handling summary.
- Procurement process: we need an approved vendor entry (vendor onboarding form), an executed MSA (legal) and then a PO. Typical timeline is 2–4 weeks for standard SaaS; longer if on-prem or custom clauses are needed.
- Decision criteria: cost/unit, latency SLOs, data isolation options, and a reference for scale.

I attached: FinTrust_org_chart_v1.pdf (internal hierarchy) and a procurement_requirements_2026.docx (procurement checklist).

Next step: I can introduce you to Maria and Tom — what would you like me to say in the intro? If you can send a short 2-line intro we can loop them in this week.

Best,
Samantha Green
Head of Platform Partnerships
FinTrust
Samantha.Green@fintrust.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@fintrust.com>, Maria.Alvarez@fintrust.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 20:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Next steps: stakeholder map & procurement path

Thanks Samantha — really helpful. Two quick asks for the intro email to Maria/Tom so we make it efficient: 

1) Can you introduce us to Maria as the economic buyer and include whether the budget is centralized (CFO) or owned by Product? Knowing the approval threshold (e.g., >$100k requires finance committee) would be helpful.
2) For Tom/legal — can he confirm the specific data handling evidence he needs (SOC 2 Type II + syslog retention policy? encryption at rest + in transit)? We’ll prep a short security summary specifically for FinTrust.

Suggested intro text (feel free to copy/paste):
"Hi Maria and Tom — following a discovery call with FinTrust Platform, Redwood Inference can materially reduce inference costs and meet your latency SLOs for summarization and chat workloads. Logan Wright (AE, cc’d) will share a brief mutual action plan and the security packet; he can be your vendor POC for next steps. Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and configurable private deployments. — Samantha"

If that works I’ll draft a 1-page MAP and a 3-slide technical summary for Tom to review. Vivek (cc’d) will own the technical demo and pilot sizing.

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Next steps: stakeholder map & procurement path

Looping in a couple of internal notes on commercial/discount approvals so you have guidance before the Maria intro:

- Standard pilot discounts (single-month or 3-month pilots) up to 20% can be approved by AE + Rev Ops sign-off. Anything >20% or multi-quarter committed discounts need manager approval (Marissa).
- If FinTrust requests price protection or a runway extension we need a short justification (expected ARR, strategic reference, product bet).
- For procurement redlines, legal will push for indemnity and data residency clauses; try to limit custom language if we want faster turnaround.

When you send the MAP, add a one-line commercial ask (e.g., target pilot budget range) so we can pre-clear approval. I can expedite once Maria’s expected spend band is visible.

-Marissa
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
